Growth.

Compare 23 September and 2 October 2026 for every warzone in the complete 1573–1636 transfer group. See who grew, how the tracked roster changed, and which servers exchanged positions within the fixed 16 / 32 / 16 state allocation.

Reading this view
Two snapshots. Fixed state counts.

Each date has exactly 16 Limited Open, 32 Semi-Open, and 16 Fully Open servers. Our ranking decides which servers fill those positions; the game's actual Warzone Score is unavailable.

METHOD / LIMITS

How to interpret the changes

1. Tracked hero power

For each warzone, compare the sum of hero power for its recorded players. The roster breakdown separates power changes among retained UIDs from the power of newly present and missing records.

2. Fixed state allocation

On each date, rank all 64 warzones in 1573–1636 using equal weights for percentile ranks of top-10 and top-50 average hero power. Ranks #1–16 are Limited Open, #17–48 Semi-Open, and #49–64 Fully Open. Crossing a rank boundary swaps another server out of that state.

3. Warzone Points proxy

Map rank and projected state to the 7 September point distribution from 1509–1572. Adjust the prior group's scale by the ratio of median August top-three alliance strength in the two groups. The same calibration is used on both snapshot dates.

The game's Warzone Score formula and future thresholds are unavailable. Server power can fall when players leave or records disappear. This is a nine-day comparison of locally saved 23 September and 2 October LWServers data. The API's v= query refreshes a mutable endpoint; requesting an older date now does not restore that snapshot.
